title: beta-funnel-orchestrator-with-observation-driven-fallbacks
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces Beta Funnel Orchestrator: observation-driven staged rollouts with live traffic inspection and automated fallbacks. Adds new metrics probes, webhook adapters, and a small controller to sequence A/B/beta cohorts. No customer-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: Several recent rollouts required manual intervention when subtle regressions were only visible under a specific traffic funnel (e.g., high-context threads). This PR introduces the Beta Funnel Orchestrator (BFO): a compact controller that sequences cohorted traffic through experimental model variants, runs inline observation probes (synthetic perturbation tests and metric assertions), and triggers automated fallback or quarantine when predefined safety gates fail.

Summary of changes: Adds controller and CRD-like config for funnel stages, a lightweight webhook adapter for running per-request inspection hooks, a new set of metric probes (response-quality, hallucination-rate proxy, latency-p50/p95 deltas), and an observability shim that correlates cohort traces with rollback decisions. Also includes SDK helpers (TS + Python) for defining funnel membership and for emitting structured inspection events to Redwood Console.

Key features: - Funnel stages with percentage/window/timebox controls and cohort selectors - Observation-driven gates: metric thresholds, percentile comparisons against baseline, and result-level heuristics (structured output validation) - Automated fallback actions: immediate revert to baseline, quarantine of suspect requests to a shadow bucket, or progressive throttling - Safety TTL: transient quaratine with auto-retry after a stabilization window - Audit trail: full decision log stored to eventstore for post-mortem and linear ticket attachments

Implementation notes: - runtime/controller/: orchestrator and scheduler, core logic implemented in Go; uses existing servegraph hooks for routing decisions - infra/observability/: metric probes and tracing adapters; integrates with existing tracing tags and cost breakdowns - sdk/ts and sdk/python: convenience APIs for cohort selection and emitting inspection events - e2e/tests: end-to-end harness simulating traffic funnels and injected regressions; includes a small chaos test to validate fallback sequencing

Commits: - 1d9f3a2: add beta funnel CRD and controller skeleton - 2a7b1c4: wire routing hooks into servegraph evaluation - 3c88b9e: implement observation gate evaluation and action executor - 4d331f0: add webhook adapter and SDK helpers - 5e6b2d1: tests + CI pipelines + docs

Changed files (high level): - runtime/controller/funnel_controller.go (new) - runtime/controller/scheduler.go (new) - runtime/controller/actions.go (new) - infra/observability/probes.go (new) - sdk/typescript/funnel.ts (new) - sdk/python/redwood/funnel.py (new) - docs/rollouts/beta-funnel.md (new) - e2e/tests/funnel_injection_test.go (new) - ci/pipeline/funnel.yml (touched)

Small illustrative snippet (routing hook): "if probe.Failures > threshold { return ActionFallbackBaseline }" — implemented as pluggable rule so ops can add heuristics without recompiling.

Testing and validation: Local unit tests and e2e harness passed. CI lint and integration jobs green (one flaky test retried once). Load tests show <5% additional median latency for inspected requests (probe execution is offloaded and sampled). Regression simulation validated automated fallback within configured SLO window.

Rollout plan: - Canary: enable BFO on internal-only cohort (10% internal traffic) for 48h - Beta: extend to customers with beta flag (5% overall) and enable full observation gates - Progressive: enable on gradual cohorts with automatic rollback enabled after gated failures - Post-merge: monitor signals via Redwood Console dashboards and run focused evaluations for top-10 flows listed in ENG-7842

Backwards compatibility and migration: No changes to public API; controller defaults are conservative (observation-only) and require explicit funnel config to take automated actions. Existing servegraph routing continues to work.

Review conversation: Marco Liu: "Solid design; prefer separation between fast inline probes vs. heavier async validators — can we ensure async path is used for structured output checks?" Aisha Patel: "Yes, heavy validators run async by default; added configuration and tests to assert async behavior." Jenna Ortiz: "Need stronger audit trail for rollback decisions so SRE can postmortem." Aisha Patel: "Added eventstore writes and linked linear anchors in the decision log; see infra/observability/eventstore.go changes." Diego Fernandez: "CI had a flaky test; re-recorded mocks and re-ran suite; all green."

Follow-ups: - ENG-7890: expose funnel health metrics in Console dashboards - ENG-7912: add UI for authoring funnel configs in Redwood Console - PM-400: product docs and customer beta onboarding checklist

Merge decision: After two approvals and green CI we merged via squash. No production incidents seen during internal canary.
